## Design Principles

<div class="principle-grid">
  <div class="principle-card">
    <h3>Clarity over breadth</h3>
    <p>The core path stays intentionally narrow so the reader does not have to fight through an oversized survey before touching real methods.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="principle-card">
    <h3>Notebook-native workflow</h3>
    <p>The website mirrors the actual repository structure, so the public site and the working lab stay aligned instead of drifting apart.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="principle-card">
    <h3>Honest maturity</h3>
    <p>Runnable pages, scaffolds, and frontier notes are not mixed together. The site should make the current state of the project legible at a glance.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="principle-card">
    <h3>Research-forward pacing</h3>
    <p>Readers can enter at foundations, jump to operator models, or scan frontier directions without losing the overall logic of the lab.</p>
  </div>
</div>

## Deployment Model

<div class="deployment-note">
  <p>
    This website is built with Quarto and deployed through GitHub Pages using GitHub Actions. Each push to <code>main</code> can render the book, upload the static site, and publish a fresh version of the lab.
  </p>
  <p>
    As more notebooks become executable and less scaffold-like, this site can evolve from a polished repo browser into a stronger teaching and research surface.
  </p>
</div>
